text: It was not until midnight. <break time="0.8s" /> That only the last stone remained. <break time="0.8s" /> And from behind the wall. <break time="0.8s" /> Came a low, sad laugh. <break time="0.8s" /> Ha, ha a very good joke indeed. <break time="0.8s" /> And we will laugh about it later. <break time="0.8s" /> Over our wine. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the voice. <break time="0.8s" /> But is it not getting late. <break time="0.8s" /> And will the others not be waiting. <break time="0.8s" /> For us at home. <break time="0.8s" /> Let us be gone. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes I answered. <break time="0.8s" /> As I lifted the last heavy stone. <break time="0.8s" /> Let us be gone. <break time="0.8s" /> For the love of God, Montresor. <break time="0.8s" /> He cried. <break time="0.8s" /> And I repeated his words. <break time="0.8s" /> Yes, for the love of God. <break time="0.8s" /> I called his name twice. <break time="0.8s" /> But there was no answer. <break time="0.8s" /> Except the soft ringing. <break time="0.8s" /> Of the bells on his cap. <break time="0.8s" /> My heart grew sick. <break time="0.8s" /> But I told myself. <break time="0.8s" /> That it was only. <break time="0.8s" /> Because of the dampness of the vaults. <break time="0.8s" /> I hurried to put the last stone. <break time="0.8s" /> In place. <break time="0.8s" /> And against the new wall. <break time="0.8s" /> I piled up the old bones again. <break time="0.8s" /> For half a century. <break time="0.8s" /> No living person. <break time="0.8s" /> Has disturbed those bones. <break time="0.8s" /> And they still keep my secret today. <break time="0.8s" /> And so I end my story. <break time="0.8s" /> With a short Latin prayer. <break time="0.8s" /> In pace requiescat. <break time="0.8s" /> Which means. <break time="0.8s" /> May he rest in peace.
